action_summary: The project's own content-only reader calls mkdir a real effect beyond its observable vocabulary. This round does not grow a sensor from those readings; it computes the smallest OS-derived field request that makes the effect testable. From one positive execution plus a stability repeat, 16 stat_result fields are priced on real controls. Three fields tie at zero false fires; st_mode is selected by printed alphabetical tie-break. The learned new-path field/value relation transfers with 0 false accepts and 0 false rejects on 8 training and 8 held rows in different trees. The old law is preserved: the sensor is requested, not invented. Two defects are reported: the first run observed before only after execution, and the naive 'new path appeared' shortcut accepts touch, write_file and symlink. No model, no parameters, no benchmark claim.

Three goals were falsified by plans: cleanliness is met by dropping the stash (destroying the work), identity with the starting commit plus preserve is unsatisfiable (204 executions, 0 solved), and the content goal was met by committing the mess onto the branch it was on until every other branch tip was pinned.
